title: Activation Energy
hook: I don't skip the gym because I'm lazy. I skip it because packing the bag feels like a project.
statement: Make starting easier. The less setup in the way, the more likely you actually begin.
explainer: Most habits die in the setup, before they ever start. Remove the friction and starting becomes almost automatic. You don't need more motivation, you need fewer steps.
sop: Pick one habit you keep meaning to do and keep skipping.
List every setup step before you can actually start.
Rate its Activation Energy from 1 to 10.
Remove or pre-do the most annoying setup step.
Re-rate Activation Energy and check your Start Probability went up.
equation_example: Activation Energy 8: 1 ÷ 8 = 0.125, about a 12.5% chance you start. Drop it to 2: 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5, a 50% chance. Higher Start Probability means starting is nearly automatic. Lower means friction wins.
question: Name one setup step you could do the night before so a habit basically starts itself.
closing_statement: Most people lack an easy start, not motivation.
caption:
Principle Nº 159: Activation Energy
